> Static distinction: the test asserts that a 16-byte buffer always forces recovery-close status=null. The implementation only emits was closed when rc.status===0, so this hosted assertion alone does NOT reproduce a false runtime receipt or prove an orphan was left open. The same test passed in one invocation and failed in another. Fixture nondeterminism is a supported inference from those hosted results and the buffer-cap assumption, not an independently reproduced root cause. Preserve the runtime outcome check; stabilize the test by deterministically inducing and observing the close failure separately from successful recovery.
> 
> Existing canonical context: https://github.com/unbraind/pm-csv/blob/188a3c62f7390a92b00a590205a86266ca09404d/.agents/pm/issues/pm-csv-158c.toon and https://github.com/unbraind/pm-csv/blob/188a3c62f7390a92b00a590205a86266ca09404d/.agents/pm/issues/pm-csv-yriu.toon require truthful recovery outcomes and deterministic/reaped test writers. Existing issue173 is the release-blocker owner, not a new duplicate issue.
> 
> Acceptance: force successful and null/nonzero recovery-close outcomes independently; verify exact receipt and item identity for each, reap delegated writers before cleanup; repeat the exact release gate under the pinned toolchain without weakening assertions. No local reproduction or deployed/runtime impact claimed here.
